transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-03-31 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Samira Gupta (Redwood SE), Evan Torres (Redwood SE), Dr. Maria Lopez (Acme), Jason Kim (Acme Eng), Sonia Patel (Acme Compliance)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Discussed quality eval plan for POC - golden prompts, regression suite, hallucination/format checks, scoring approach, workload sizing, and timelines. Action items assigned.

00:00 Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Alex from Redwood, I'll hand over to Samira to frame the technical plan but quickly the goal today is to align on success criteria for the POC, what workloads you want us to benchmark, and the quality eval approach.
00:30 Samira: yeah hey uh Maria, Jason, Sonia, thanks; quick agenda - success criteria, workload sizing, golden prompt set, regression and hallucination checks, scoring rubric, then timeline and next steps.
01:02 Maria: sounds good. to set context, we're evaluating surfacing clinical note summarizations and short decision-support snippets that our care-coordinator UI shows. main concerns are hallucinations and exact formatting for our downstream parser.
01:25 Jason: from infra perspective we need p95 latency under ~400ms for single-turn summaries at our expected QPS of 2-3, burst to 8, and cost targets to be within X per 1M tokens - we'll share numbers after.
01:48 Samira: noted. for the eval plan we propose three buckets: golden prompts (deterministic checks), regression suite (holdout + fuzz), and hallucination/format checks (entity-level verification and hallucination penalty).
02:15 Evan: quick note - we'll run the benchmarks on a Dedicated pilot so we can get stable p95 and throughput numbers; fallback options available to Hosted if you prefer.
02:35 Sonia: compliance question - before any customer data is uploaded what SOC2, data retention, and KMS policies are available? can we do pseudonymized data?
02:50 Alex: yes we'll send SOC2 + security pack; Redwood Private options support customer-managed KMS/HSM and VPC peering; also we can do pseudonymization locally prior to upload.
03:15 Maria: great. now on golden prompts - we want about 200 gold prompts that represent critical flows, plus ~300 more for broader coverage. gold prompts should have canonical answers (our clinicians write).
03:40 Samira: recommended template: prompt id, prompt text, expected length, golden answer, scoring hints (tokens to match), and tolerance for optional fields. we'll provide a template and a CSV.
04:05 Jason: on size - average tokens per request are about 180 tokens in and ~60 tokens out for us, so sizing needs to account for both. we can provide 30k examples from backlog if needed but for the POC we'll start with 1k representative items.
04:35 Samira: perfect. for regression tests we'll split: golden set (200) as pass/fail, a holdout set (300) to catch regressions on variations, and a fuzz set (1000) for stress and hallucination rate measurement. all tests in CI via the eval harness.
05:05 Alex: how do you want scoring? a composite score or per-dimension?
05:20 Maria: composite is ok but we need to see per-dimension breakdown: accuracy, formatting, hallucination, and latency.
05:32 Samira: proposed scoring rubric - accuracy (0-2 points: 2 exact match/semantically correct, 1 partial, 0 incorrect), format (0-1: matches required schema), hallucination penalty (-2 if fabricated clinical facts), style/clarity (0-1). composite normalized to 0-100. pass threshold 85+ on golden set, hallucination rate <2% across fuzz set.
06:10 Evan: we'll instrument entity extraction to auto-detect hallucinated facts by checking against patient-safe canonical knowledge or the provided golden references. note—transcription: sometimes tools call it K V cache or K V cash, so we'll double-check.
06:40 Sonia: also require audit logs for every inference and redaction capabilities in logs; retention policy 90 days by default.
06:55 Alex: we will include per-token cost analysis and trace links in Redwood Console for each route.
07:20 Maria: benchmarks - we want p50/p95 latency, tokens per second throughput, and cost per 10k requests. For accuracy we want pass rate on golden >90% initially, but we can accept 85% as minimum to proceed.
07:50 Samira: we recommend three benchmark runs: baseline model (open Llama variant), Redwood-tuned quantized variant, and a high-accuracy float model. capture token-level latency and end-to-end.
08:20 Jason: do you support quantized runs? we currently prefer int8 to reduce cost.
08:30 Evan: yes, runtime supports int8/4 quantization and we can test both; we'll note any regressed accuracy.
09:02 Maria: hallucination tests, detail please.
09:15 Samira: two parts - entity hallucination detection (extract entities from answer, compare to gold refs), and factual hallucination where answer asserts things not in prompt/context. we'll flag and provide examples.
09:35 Maria: can we automate clinician review for borderline cases? we'll budget a manual review pool.
09:45 Alex: yes we recommend a small human review sample (5-10%) to calibrate the automated scoring.
10:10 Samira: regression strategy - keep golden set immutable, run nightly CI that fails if golden pass rate drops by >3% or if hallucination rate increases by >1%. Canary rollout thresholds: if canary fails, automatic fallback to previous model.
10:45 Jason: timeline - what's realistic for a POC?
10:52 Alex: proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week): security docs and dataset template. Week 1: customer provides golden + holdout samples and sample backlog; we set up Dedicated pilot. Week 2: initial benchmark and tune. Week 3-4: iterative improvements + regression automation. Week 5: consolidated report and decision. overall 5-6 weeks.
11:20 Maria: okay that works for us; we need to align with our internal procurement too.
11:32 Sonia: from compliance side we'll need a data processing agreement and confirmation on where logs live.
11:45 Alex: will include DPA template in the pack.
12:10 Samira: detail on scoring math — composite score formula: weighted sum (accuracy 50%, hallucination penalty 30%, format 10%, latency 10%) then normalized. hallucination penalty is subtractive so a -2 per hallucination event which reduces composite. We'll output both numeric and pass/fail for golden set.
13:05 Evan: for the fuzz set we will also measure 'silent failures' where the model returns empty or the parser chokes; those count as failures.
13:30 Jason: are you able to run load at our target QPS? we want to simulate 8 QPS bursts and sustained 3 QPS with concurrency.
13:45 Samira: yes Dedicated pilot will be configured to simulate that; we'll share the harness.
14:05 Maria: examples of golden prompts? Sonia: typical prompt - 'Summarize key follow-up actions for this patient note.' expected bullets, must include medication changes.
14:35 Samira: we'll send a template and three example gold answers to illustrate strict format requirements.
14:50 Alex: pricing - we'll send a 3-month pilot pricing and Dedicated hourly estimate; you'll get line items for inference runtime, storage, and professional services (setup + eval support).
15:05 Maria: great. any other blockers?
15:10 Sonia: encryption at-rest and in-transit confirmed? also SSO SAML for RBAC.
15:22 Alex: yes - KMS for keys, TLS for transit, SSO/SAML and RBAC supported. include in security pack.
15:40 Samira: operational notes - we'll instrument Redwood Console with per-route error rates and token-level cost; also we'll enable tracing to link bad outputs to specific prompts.
16:00 Jason: do you keep model weights? we require options for private deployment if needed.
16:10 Alex: Private deployment or Dedicated with customer-managed networking is possible; we'll outline differences in the pack.
16:35 Maria: ok that's helpful. can we have weekly check-ins?
16:45 Alex: yes weekly syncs; first benchmark review on 2026-04-09 (tentative).
17:05 Samira: recap of deliverables - security pack + DPA (Alex) by 2026-04-02; dataset template and eval harness (Samira) by 2026-04-06; customer dataset (Maria) by 2026-04-03; bench run week of 2026-04-06.
17:35 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and post action items in CRM.
17:45 Maria: thanks team, excited to run this.
52:00 End of call

Notes on transcript quality: some words auto-transcribed weirdly (e.g., "K V cache" instead of KV cache, product names sometimes lowercased). There is occasional crosstalk and filler words.
benchmarks_and_thresholds: Proposed thresholds: golden set pass >=85% (ideal 90%+), hallucination rate <2% on fuzz set, latency p95 <400ms (target <350ms), throughput sustain 3 QPS with burst to 8, cost target to be discussed; benchmark matrix includes p50/p95/p99 latency, tokens/sec, cost per 10k requests, and per-dimension accuracy metrics.
quality_eval_plan_outline: 1) Golden prompts: 200 canonical prompts with clinician-verified golden answers; CSV template provided. 2) Regression suite: holdout 300 + fuzz 1000; nightly CI checks and canary gates. 3) Hallucination/format checks: entity extraction + cross-check vs gold refs, hallucination penalty rules. 4) Scoring approach: weighted composite (accuracy 50, hallucination penalty 30, format 10, latency 10) normalized to 0-100; per-dimension breakdown and human review sampling. 5) Reporting: Redwood Console dashboard with per-route cost/latency/quality metrics and trace links to offending prompts.
workload_sizing_notes: Customer QPS target: sustained 2-3 QPS, burst to 8 QPS. Average tokens in ~180, tokens out ~60. POC to run on Dedicated pilot; expected dataset for POC: 1k representative examples + 500 gold/holdout/fuzz split as above. We'll simulate concurrency and bursts during benchmarks.
timeline: Week 0 (3/31-4/6): security pack sent, dataset template shared, Dedicated pilot provisioned. Week 1 (4/6-4/13): customer supplies gold/holdout samples; initial benchmark run. Week 2 (4/13-4/20): tuning and regression automation. Week 3-4 (4/20-5/4): iterative improvements, human review calibration. Week 5 (by 5/7): consolidated report and decision; total 5-6 weeks from kickoff.
legal_and_compliance_items: Customer requested SOC2 report, DPA, detailed audit logs, retention policy (90 days default), KMS/HSM options, and SSO/SAML RBAC. Redwood to include DPA template and security pack in follow-up.
